research_domain_title: Assistance, Security, Participation, and Pathways to Independence
note: Major pillar architecture. Rejects one-size-fits-all assistance and UBI as the alternative. Distinguishes security from dependency. Exact benefit phaseout rates require modeling (modeling remains 0%). Empirical SNAP scale claim is sourced; pathway design and program redesign remain architecture until researched and piloted.
role_in_philosophy: Assistance should protect people who cannot provide for themselves, stabilize people in temporary crisis, remove barriers for those who can work, and create a believable path from public support to income, ownership, and full community participation — not manage a dependent population.

rejected_framing.text: Everyone receiving government assistance has the same problem.
rejected_framing.reason: A retired worker on Social Security, a disabled adult, a mother caring for an infant, a worker earning poverty wages, a person recovering from addiction, and an able-bodied adult disconnected from work require entirely different responses.

organizing_principle.text: No person should be abandoned when unable to meet essential needs. No institution should trap a capable person in dependency. Assistance should protect dignity, strengthen capacity, reward productive advancement, and lead toward the greatest independence reasonably possible.

security_vs_dependency.security: A person knows that hunger, illness, disability, childhood, caregiving, or temporary job loss will not destroy their life.
security_vs_dependency.dependency: Program rules make it financially dangerous to work more, marry, save, accept a promotion, start a business, or accumulate property.

objective.text: Protect people who cannot provide for themselves, stabilize people in temporary crisis, remove barriers for those who can work, and create a believable path from public support to income, ownership, and full community participation.

scale_context.summary: SNAP alone served an average of 41.7 million people per month in fiscal year 2024—about 12.3% of the population. That illustrates scale, but does not mean 41.7 million people are permanently disconnected from work; SNAP serves children, older adults, disabled people, low-wage workers, and households experiencing temporary hardship.
scale_context.note: Scale context only — not a locked national program redesign claim.

pathways.title: Permanent protection
pathways.summary: For substantial disability, severe chronic illness, advanced age without adequate resources, or permanent incapacity — stable support without repeated humiliating re-proof of permanent conditions; encourage voluntary participation without threatening essential healthcare or housing.

pathways.title: Childhood and dependent care
pathways.summary: Children are not welfare recipients in the moral sense; ensure food, healthcare, safe housing, education, transportation, and developmental support. Parents remain primarily responsible; no child is deprived because adults cannot or will not meet an essential need.

pathways.title: Caregiving
pathways.summary: Verified caregiving for a young child, disabled family member, seriously ill spouse, or elderly parent is productive social participation — not idleness.

pathways.title: Temporary stabilization
pathways.summary: Immediate, simple, time-limited support for job loss, illness, divorce, disaster, housing disruption, or short-term family crisis, with a recovery plan that begins at enrollment.

pathways.title: Working but economically insecure
pathways.summary: Solution is wages, scheduling, childcare, transportation, healthcare, training, worker representation, and employer accountability — not punishment. Public assistance should not become a permanent wage subsidy for large profitable corporations.

pathways.title: Capable but disconnected
pathways.summary: Active engagement and an individualized route into treatment, education, employment, public service, apprenticeship, community restoration, or supported work. Support remains available; participation becomes reciprocal once barriers have been addressed.

benefit_cliff.rule: Every additional hour of productive work should leave a household better off.
benefit_cliff.definition_note: Federal researchers define a benefit cliff as a situation in which lost benefits equal or exceed the earnings increase that triggered the reduction; CBO treats benefit phaseouts as part of the effective marginal tax rate workers face.
benefit_cliff.design: Benefits should decline gradually so total household resources always rise when earned income rises. Exact rates vary by program and require modeling.
benefit_cliff.transparency: Recipients should see current earnings, expected raise, taxes, gradually reduced assistance, and new household income before accepting a promotion or additional hours. Universal benefit-impact calculators should be integrated into every recipient account.
benefit_cliff.modeling_note: Phaseout rate calibration is modeling work — modeling remains 0%; architecture only.

human_prosperity_account.summary: One secure account coordinating fragmented programs — benefits, eligibility dates, income, work and training, phaseout schedule, appointments, services, goals, local opportunities, progress toward independence, and appeal rights — with one accountable local navigator.
human_prosperity_account.privacy_rule: Technology coordinates programs; it must not create a surveillance system. Access limited, logged, and governed by strict privacy rules.

prosperity_navigators.summary: Replace case processing with prosperity planning. Technology handles eligibility calculations, reminders, coordination, duplicate detection, income updates, and routine renewals. Human workers become Prosperity Navigators focused on barriers, capacities, local economy needs, durable routes forward, service step-down, and ownership accumulation.
prosperity_navigators.iconic_phrase: Automate the routine. Elevate the human.

foundations_of_participation.summary: Before imposing participation requirements, address childcare, transportation, identification, literacy, healthcare, mental health, addiction, housing stability, internet access, criminal-record barriers, disability accommodation, and local job availability.
foundations_of_participation.sanction_limits: A person cannot reasonably be sanctioned for failing to take a job that does not exist, cannot be reached, pays less than childcare cost, jeopardizes necessary medical coverage, or cannot accommodate a disability.
foundations_of_participation.evaluation_note: CBO finds effects of work requirements and work supports vary and can be uncertain; requirements must be paired with genuine supports and independently evaluated.

forms_of_contribution.standard: Are you actively moving toward the greatest degree of independence and contribution available to you?

community_work_guarantee.summary: Explicit alternative to universal basic income: any adult capable of contributing but unable to find suitable private employment should be offered a paid local public or community assignment — real transitional jobs with wages, expectations, supervision, training, worker protections, and pathways into private employment or public service.
community_work_guarantee.rejects: universal basic income as the organizing alternative
constraints: must not become punitive work camps
community_work_guarantee.message: If the private market has no place for your available capacity today, the community will help you build value while you prepare for the next opportunity.

employer_responsibility.summary: Measure which large employers have substantial numbers of full-time workers depending on public benefits. Profitable corporations paying below the realistic cost of sustaining their workforce shift labor costs onto taxpayers.
responses: low-wage employer assessment based on company-wide practices
employer_responsibility.anti_discrimination_guardrail: Assessment should not be tied to the benefit status of named workers, which could encourage employers to avoid hiring vulnerable people.

asset_building.summary: Reverse rules that punish saving, reliable vehicles, emergency reserves, business starts, or productive equipment. Encourage emergency savings, retirement assets, education accounts, business capital, home equity, tools, transportation, and cooperative ownership — including matched Prosperity Accounts.
asset_building.destination: Acquire enough income and ownership that people are unlikely to need benefits again — not merely exit a roll.

barriers_requiring_action.summary: Treat addiction, illness, and homelessness as barriers requiring coordinated action — crisis stabilization, treatment, transitional housing, supervised recovery, identification, employment, transportation, and mentors — not abandonment waiting for serious offense.
barriers_requiring_action.compulsion_rule: Participation may be compulsory only in narrowly defined situations involving serious danger, repeated criminal behavior, or incapacity, with due process and professional review.
twin_errors: Support without expectations can become abandonment.
Punishment without treatment can become an expensive revolving door.

reciprocity.summary: After a realistic pathway is offered, an able adult who repeatedly refuses every reasonable opportunity should not receive the same unrestricted support indefinitely.
consequence_rules: never eliminate emergency food, shelter, or lifesaving care

fraud_and_burden.summary: Eliminate fraud without treating everyone as fraudulent. Use verified identity, integrated income reporting, duplicate detection, employer reporting, audit sampling, cross-program consistency, due process, and meaningful penalties for organized fraud — without constant humiliation for lawful recipients.
fraud_and_burden.burden_note: Administrative burden itself can destabilize families. HHS research identifies repeated reapplication, job instability, and benefit loss as significant sources of economic risk for low-income households.

exit_measurement.success_question: Did the person become more capable, secure, independent, and connected to the community?

governing_promise.text: We will feed the hungry, protect children, care for the disabled, honor caregivers, stabilize families in crisis, and refuse to abandon people suffering from illness or addiction. In return, every person capable of contributing will be offered a meaningful pathway to work, service, learning, recovery, ownership, and citizenship. Assistance will never punish advancement, and it will never be designed as a permanent substitute for human potential.
governing_promise.destination: Not by indiscriminately cutting people off and not by warehousing them in dependency—but by replacing a fragmented welfare bureaucracy with a coordinated human-development system whose destination is security, contribution, and ownership.

assistance_test.title: Constitutional Assistance Test
assistance_test.purpose: Screen assistance and workforce proposals for pathway differentiation, security-without-dependency, anti-cliff design, barrier removal before sanctions, reciprocity fairness, and honest exit measurement.

questions.text: Does this place recipients on the correct pathway rather than treating all assistance cases as the same problem?
Does it guarantee security for people who cannot provide for themselves while dismantling rules that trap capable people in dependency?
Does every additional hour of productive work leave the household better off — with gradual phaseouts rather than benefit cliffs?
Are participation requirements paired with genuine supports (childcare, transport, health, housing, treatment, local jobs), and never used to sanction impossible jobs?
Does it recognize caregiving, recovery, education, and community contribution — not paycheck alone — as movement toward independence?
If private employment is unavailable, does it offer a Community Work Guarantee rather than substituting universal basic income as the organizing answer?
Do profitable large employers carry their share without assessments that punish hiring named benefit recipients?
Does assistance encourage asset-building and ownership, and measure success by capability, security, independence, and community connection — not roll exit alone?
Are consequences for refusal gradual, appealable, proportionate, never imposed on children, and never allowed to eliminate emergency food, shelter, or lifesaving care?
Does fraud control target organized abuse without constant humiliation of lawful recipients or destabilizing administrative burden?
